chunks: “If the miscarried fetus has completed four months, it is to be washed.” And he said: “If it has completed six months, then it is complete, and that is because al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام was born when he was a son of six months.” So his specification, عليه السلام, of washing the miscarried fetus when it has reached four months and beyond indicates that if it is less than that, then its washing is not obligatory. And this meaning is indicated by this.

(961) 129 — What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:
I wrote to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام asking him about the miscarried fetus, how it should be dealt with. So he wrote back to me: “The miscarried fetus is buried with its blood in its place.”

key_terms.بِدَمِهِ: with its blood, without washing it off in this context
key_terms.تَامٌّ: complete in bodily formation or term in this legal context
key_terms.سِتَّةُ أَشْهُرٍ: six months, indicating a completed and viable term in this context
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: it is given ghusl (ritual washing for the dead)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing and burying a miscarried fetus in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling concerning a miscarried fetus, distinguishing between stages of gestation in relation to ghusl. It also reports that a miscarried fetus is buried with its blood in the place where it is found, while noting that completion of four months carries a distinct legal consequence.
